mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level (FEDFUNDS) is causally associated with higher 5-day S&P 500 forward returns, as lower rates reduce the discount rate applied to equity valuations.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5% compared to the average return over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals a weakening labor market that leads to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings face downward pressure.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) when UNRATE > 4.0% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5% over the past three months signals a broad-based economic slowdown that leads to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both decline > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) when both INDPRO and HOUST decline by more than 0.5% in the last 3 months over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in retail sales (RSAFS) signals an impending economic slowdown that leads to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as consumer spending weakens.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) when RSAFS declines by more than 0.5% in a late-cycle expansion regime over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher housing starts level (HOUST) is causally associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns, as it signals strong consumer demand and economic activity.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in the top 25% of HOUST observations over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 2.5% signals an inflationary shock that leads to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as the Federal Reserve may tighten policy.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) when CPIAUCSL y/y > 2.5% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In an early-cycle expansion regime, a slowdown in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) signals a potential economic deceleration that leads to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) when PAYEMS growth rate < 0.5% in an early-cycle expansion regime over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a tightening monetary policy that leads to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) when FEDFUNDS > 1.5% and CPIAUCSL y/y > 2.0% over any 3-year rolling window.
